name: Tetserret
world_status: statement found in an open source
sweep_summary: Tetserret is not in the catalog. The single sweep item, Lux & Philippson 2010 (Études berbères V, Berber Studies 28, pp. 133-164), is confirmed as a first-hand word-stress study of Tetserret (publisher TOC and Glottolog record saved) but exists only as a paid Köppe PDF/print (no DOI, no open copy on HAL, OpenAlex, Crossref, Google Books, archive.org, DDL Lyon or HathiTrust). Its content is recoverable first-hand: Lux's open 2011 Lyon 2 thesis (already on file, archive.org) states in footnote 174 (p. 251) that its chapter 4 reproduces that article, and gives the rules — nouns: masculine default antepenult, feminine default penult (p. 267); verbs: aorist first syllable, perfective final syllable, imperfective first stem vowel, negative perfective retracted to the verb's first syllable (pp. 280-284); summary table 83 p. 290; Tetserret's grammatical accent contrasts with Tamacheq's demarcative antepenult. p. 135 restates the same rules), the Köppe records for Berber Studies 28 and 38, and the Glottolog reference record; Kossmann 2020 (on file) independently cites Lux 2013: 284ff. for aorist-initial vs perfective-second-syllable accent. Lux 2014 (STUF) is intonation of focus, not word stress. Acquiring the 2010 article itself is medium priority (content already in hand via the thesis); best available statement: thesis pp. 267/280.

earlier_scan.source_named: Lux, Cecile. 2011/2013. Etude descriptive et comparative d'une langue menacee: le tetserret, langue berbere du Niger (PhD Lyon 2 / Berber Studies vol. 38); not reachable online

new_statements.quote: En tetserret, en revanche, l’accent est très clairement grammatical [...] (p. 264) On peut donc affirmer que les nominaux masculins, en tetserret, sont accentués par défaut sur la syllabe antépénultième, quand la longueur du nom le permet, alors que les nominaux féminins sont accentués par défaut sur la syllabe pénultième. (p. 267) La règle accentuelle générale pour le verbe, en tetserret, est que chacun des trois aspects est accentué différemment [...] On retrouve donc, en tetserret, l'opposition [...] entre aoriste accentué sur la première syllabe du verbe et accompli accentué sur la syllabe finale. (p. 280)
new_statements.translation: In Tetserret, by contrast, the accent is very clearly grammatical [...] One can thus state that masculine nominals in Tetserret are accented by default on the antepenultimate syllable, when the length of the noun allows it, whereas feminine nominals are accented by default on the penultimate syllable. The general accentual rule for the verb in Tetserret is that each of the three aspects is accented differently [...] One thus finds in Tetserret the opposition [...] between the aorist accented on the first syllable of the verb and the perfective accented on the final syllable.
new_statements.citation: Lux, Cécile. 2011. Étude descriptive et comparative d'une langue menacée : le tetserret, langue berbère du Niger. Thèse de doctorat, Université Lumière Lyon 2 (dir. G. Philippson). Ch. 4 'Prosodie : système accentuel et intonation', §4.2.1.1.1 and §4.2.2.1.1.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Word accent exists and is grammatically (morphologically) conditioned rather than fixed: nouns in isolation -- masculine nouns take antepenultimate accent by default (penult if only disyllabic; when a plural suffix adds a syllable the accent lands on the new antepenult), feminine nouns take penultimate accent whatever their length; verbs -- aorist/imperative accented on the first syllable of the verb, perfective on the final syllable, imperfective on the first vowel of the stem, negative perfective (after wər) on the first syllable of the verb (prefix included). Accent is realized by raised F0 plus lengthening and intensity of the accented vowel.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Not discussed; no secondary accent described in ch. 4.
new_statements.exceptions: Unassimilated loanwords (French, Arabic, Songhay, Tamasheq) are accented on the penult; a handful of unexplained lexical exceptions (e.g. t-mddkkel-t 'amie', y 'lune', t-mog 'fille'); with possessive and demonstrative clitics the default rules are neutralized (singular possessive clitics attract the accent); preverbal particles d-, ar, har attract the accent in the aorist; with verbal clitics accentuation is 'très irrégulière'; author flags syllabification as uncertain (fn. 194) and calls this a first study of the accent (fn. 195).
new_statements.domain_note: Described for nouns and verbs in isolation and with clitics, from a field corpus of texts; the noun's accent domain is limited to the noun itself (never shifts onto a preceding preposition), unlike Tamasheq where the domain is the accentual group/NP; intonation contours (§4.3) can override/perturb word accent.
new_statements.identity_note: Lux's corpus is Tetserret as spoken by the Ayttawari Seslem (Azawagh, Niger), i.e. tets1235 proper; the closely related Kel Eghlal n-Enniger variety (tamesgelalt/'tamsghlalt', described by Drouin 1984) is treated by Lux as a dialect of Tetserret and is not separately analysed for accent. The comparison language throughout ch. 4 is Tamasheq (Tawellemmet/Tayert), whose antepenultimate demarcative accent must not be confused with the Tetserret rules.

[...] The general accent rule for the verb in Tetserret is that each of the three aspects is accented differently [...] between the aorist accented on the first syllable of the verb and the perfective accented on the final syllable.
new_statements.citation: Lux, Cécile. 2011. Étude descriptive et comparative d'une langue menacée : le tetserret, langue berbère du Niger. Thèse de doctorat, Université Lumière Lyon 2, ch. 4 (the chapter that, per footnote 174 p. 251, reproduces Lux & Philippson 2010, 'L'accent en tetserret et en tamacheq').
new_statements.locator: printed p. 267 (PDF p. 266), sec. 4.2.1.1.1, and printed p. 280 (PDF p. 279), secs. 4.2.2.1.1-4.2.2.1.1.1; summary table 83 printed p. 290 (PDF p. 289)
new_statements.reading: Tetserret has a word-bounded, morphologically governed accent (the author's 'accent morphologique/grammatical'), not a fixed-position demarcative stress: nouns take antepenult (masculine) or penult (feminine) by default with lexical exceptions (unassimilated loans penult), and verbs mark aspect by accent position (aorist initial, perfective final, imperfective stem-initial, negative perfective retracted to the verb's first syllable); possessive/demonstrative clitics neutralise the noun defaults. A catalog coding would be 'morphologically conditioned / gender- and aspect-determined position', with the noun default antepenult/penult by gender as the isolation rule.

sources.citation: Sarvasy, Hannah. 2017. Review of Cécile Lux, Le tetserret, langue berbère du Niger (Berber Studies 38, 2013). Journal of African Languages and Linguistics 38(1): 133–137. DOI 10.1515/jall-2017-0005.
sources.quote: Tetserret accent is placed differently on masculine (antepenult) and feminine (penult) nouns, while Tamacheq nouns of both genders have default accent placement on the antepenult. In verbs, Tetserret accent occurs on the first syllable in the aorist, the last syllable in the perfective, and the first syllable of the verb root in the imperfective.
sources.note: Second-hand summary of the prosody chapter of Lux 2013 (the published version of the thesis): accent placement in Tetserret and Tamacheq has not converged; Tetserret masculine nouns antepenult, feminine penult; verbs aorist first syllable, perfective last syllable, imperfective first syllable of the root; Tamacheq default antepenult in both nouns and verbs.
